You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE Breeds (
    breed_code VARCHAR(10)   PRIMARY KEY,
    breed_name VARCHAR(80),
    UNIQUE (breed_code)
);

CREATE TABLE Charges (
    charge_id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    charge_type VARCHAR(10),
    charge_amount DECIMAL(19,4)
);

CREATE TABLE Sizes (
    size_code VARCHAR(10)   PRIMARY KEY,
    size_description VARCHAR(80),
    UNIQUE (size_code)
);

CREATE TABLE Treatment_Types (
    treatment_type_code VARCHAR(10)   PRIMARY KEY,
    treatment_type_description VARCHAR(80),
    UNIQUE (treatment_type_code)
);

CREATE TABLE Owners (
    owner_id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name VARCHAR(50),
    last_name VARCHAR(50),
    street VARCHAR(50),
    city VARCHAR(50),
    state VARCHAR(20),
    zip_code VARCHAR(20),
    email_address VARCHAR(50),
    home_phone VARCHAR(20),
    cell_number VARCHAR(20)
);

CREATE TABLE Dogs (
    dog_id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    owner_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    abandoned_yn VARCHAR(1),
    breed_code VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
    size_code VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
    name VARCHAR(50),
    age VARCHAR(20),
    date_of_birth DATETIME,
    gender VARCHAR(1),
    weight VARCHAR(20),
    date_arrived DATETIME,
    date_adopted DATETIME,
    date_departed DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY (owner_id) REFERENCES Owners(owner_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (owner_id) REFERENCES Owners(owner_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (size_code) REFERENCES Sizes(size_code),
    FOREIGN KEY (breed_code) REFERENCES Breeds(breed_code)
);

CREATE TABLE Professionals (
    professional_id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    role_code VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
    first_name VARCHAR(50),
    street VARCHAR(50),
    city VARCHAR(50),
    state VARCHAR(20),
    zip_code VARCHAR(20),
    last_name VARCHAR(50),
    email_address VARCHAR(50),
    home_phone VARCHAR(20),
    cell_number VARCHAR(20)
);

CREATE TABLE Treatments (
    treatment_id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    dog_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    professional_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    treatment_type_code VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
    date_of_treatment DATETIME,
    cost_of_treatment DECIMAL(19,4),
    FOREIGN KEY (dog_id) REFERENCES Dogs(dog_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (professional_id) REFERENCES Professionals(professional_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (treatment_type_code) REFERENCES Treatment_Types(treatment_type_code)
);

What kind of “professionals’ analysis” do you need—schema/data profiling, operational metrics, or something else?

Here are a few common SQL analyses for the `Professionals` table (and related `Treatments`). Tell me which you want and any filters (date range, role_code, state, etc.):

### 1) Professionals list + contact completeness
```sql
SELECT
  professional_id,
  role_code,
  first_name,
  last_name,
  email_address,
  home_phone,
  cell_number,
  CASE WHEN email_address IS NULL OR email_address = '' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS has_email,
  CASE WHEN (home_phone IS NULL OR home_phone = '')
        AND (cell_number IS NULL OR cell_number = '') THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS has_phone
FROM Professionals
ORDER BY role_code, last_name, first_name;
```

### 2) Treatments per professional (workload)
```sql
SELECT
  p.professional_id,
  p.role_code,
  p.last_name,
  p.first_name,
  COUNT(t.treatment_id) AS treatment_count
FROM Professionals p
LEFT JOIN Treatments t
  ON t.professional_id = p.professional_id
GROUP BY p.professional_id, p.role_code, p.last_name, p.first_name
ORDER BY treatment_count DESC;
```

### 3) Revenue/cost totals per professional
```sql
SELECT
  p.professional_id,
  p.role_code,
  p.last_name,
  p.first_name,
  COUNT(t.treatment_id) AS treatment_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(t.cost_of_treatment), 0) AS total_cost,
  COALESCE(AVG(t.cost_of_treatment), 0) AS avg_cost
FROM Professionals p
LEFT JOIN Treatments t
  ON t.professional_id = p.professional_id
GROUP BY p.professional_id, p.role_code, p.last_name, p.first_name
ORDER BY total_cost DESC;
```

### 4) Activity by month (trend)
```sql
SELECT
  p.professional_id,
  p.last_name,
  p.first_name,
  DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(t.date_of_treatment), MONTH(t.date_of_treatment), 1) AS month_start,
  COUNT(*) AS treatments
FROM Treatments t
JOIN Professionals p
  ON p.professional_id = t.professional_id
GROUP BY
  p.professional_id, p.last_name, p.first_name,
  DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(t.date_of_treatment), MONTH(t.date_of_treatment), 1)
ORDER BY p.professional_id, month_start;
```

Which output are you looking for, and what SQL dialect are you using (SQL Server, MySQL, SQLite, PostgreSQL)?
I only want the professionals who have done at least two treatments.

```sql
SELECT
  p.professional_id,
  p.role_code,
  p.first_name,
  p.last_name,
  COUNT(t.treatment_id) AS treatment_count
FROM Professionals p
JOIN Treatments t
  ON t.professional_id = p.professional_id
GROUP BY
  p.professional_id, p.role_code, p.first_name, p.last_name
HAVING COUNT(t.treatment_id) >= 2
ORDER BY treatment_count DESC, p.last_name, p.first_name;
```
also need to include their role in the results

```sql
SELECT
  p.professional_id,
  p.role_code AS role,
  p.first_name,
  p.last_name,
  COUNT(t.treatment_id) AS treatment_count
FROM Professionals p
JOIN Treatments t
  ON t.professional_id = p.professional_id
GROUP BY
  p.professional_id, p.role_code, p.first_name, p.last_name
HAVING COUNT(t.treatment_id) >= 2
ORDER BY treatment_count DESC, p.role_code, p.last_name, p.first_name;
```
make sure to return the ID of each professional in the results.

```sql
SELECT
  p.professional_id,
  p.role_code AS role,
  p.first_name,
  p.last_name,
  COUNT(t.treatment_id) AS treatment_count
FROM Professionals p
JOIN Treatments t
  ON t.professional_id = p.professional_id
GROUP BY
  p.professional_id, p.role_code, p.first_name, p.last_name
HAVING COUNT(t.treatment_id) >= 2
ORDER BY treatment_count DESC, p.professional_id;
```
make sure to also include each professional's first name in the results.

```sql
SELECT
  p.professional_id,
  p.role_code AS role,
  p.first_name,
  p.last_name,
  COUNT(t.treatment_id) AS treatment_count
FROM Professionals p
JOIN Treatments t
  ON t.professional_id = p.professional_id
GROUP BY
  p.professional_id, p.role_code, p.first_name, p.last_name
HAVING COUNT(t.treatment_id) >= 2
ORDER BY treatment_count DESC, p.professional_id;
```
